description: Cluster live: the observability basics of one Kubernetes namespace (shop by default: set yours in Parameters), refreshing every 15 s, with nothing to run or set up. Services: requests/s, the 5xx error ratio, p50 and p99 latency per service from Prometheus (RED), each with its usual band (the median of the 30 minutes before ± 3 × MAD) and the same time yesterday; points outside the band are red, with a note in plain words ("p99 for checkout is 3.1× its usual level since 14:02"). Workloads: CPU and memory against their requests and limits, restarts, and a short forecast (Holt's linear smoothing) of every pod's memory against its limit, every volume against its capacity and every node against what it can allocate ("memory limit reached in ~40 min"). Pod phases, and the log rate per app from Loki. Deploy markers come from the rollouts (Kubernetes ReplicaSets, found as in "Did the deploy do it?"). Hover a point for its value, usual band, yesterday and the pods behind it; click a service or workload to drill down to its pods, events and log lines in the same view; expand to the same metric on the other services, and to the nodes it runs on. SAMPLE DATA: signed out, or before you connect, the three datasources read a made-up cluster that moves with the clock (generated from a model by scripts/cluster-live-sample.mjs, labelled as sample everywhere). Connect your cluster to run on yours, one of three ways: (1) the Seebra desktop app reads localhost directly: kubectl port-forward -n monitoring svc/prometheus-operated 9090, kubectl port-forward -n monitoring svc/loki 3100 and kubectl proxy --port=8001, then set the datasources to http://localhost:9090/api/v1, http://localhost:8001 and http://localhost:3100/loki/api/v1; (2) your organisation's own Seebra gateway, in the cluster: https://kubernetes.default.svc with a read-only token, and your in-cluster Prometheus or Thanos querier and Loki (on OpenShift https://thanos-querier.openshift-monitoring.svc:9091/api/v1 with a bearer token); (3) in a browser, the same localhost URLs behind a proxy that adds CORS headers (kubectl proxy and Loki send none; Prometheus has --web.cors.origin). Then set namespace and, if your metric names differ, the PromQL in Parameters: the defaults follow kube-prometheus-stack (cAdvisor, kube-state-metrics, its namespace_workload_pod:kube_pod_owner:relabel and node_namespace_pod_container recording rules) and OpenTelemetry's http_server_request_duration_seconds histogram for requests, which your apps export (kube-prometheus-stack doesn't measure requests itself). Read only: nothing here writes to the cluster. Caveats: points are 1-minute rates every 15 s, so neighbouring points are not independent and short spikes are smoothed; histogram_quantile interpolates within buckets; the band learns from the last 30 minutes only (a slow drift becomes usual; yesterday is the check); a forecast says what happens if the recent trend holds, nothing more; memory is per pod against the sum of its containers' limits (an OOM kill is per container); events expire (an hour by default); Loki returns at most 1000 lines.
name: Cluster live
